title: Redundant Connection Problem

content.problemStatement:
A graph started out as a tree with `n` nodes, labeled 1 to `n`, connected
by `n`-1 edges. One extra edge was then added, connecting two nodes that
were already connected, which created exactly one cycle. You're given the
list of `n` edges in the order they were added (each edge is a pair
[u, v]).

**Return the edge that can be removed to turn the graph back into a tree.**

If more than one edge could be removed to achieve this, return the one that appears last in the input list.
constraints: the input describes a tree plus exactly one extra edge
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: 1-2 and 1-3 already connect all three nodes; 2-3 closes the cycle
1-2-3-4 already forms a path; adding 1-4 closes it into a cycle
1 is already connected to 2, 3, and 4; adding 3-4 closes a cycle

hints: Model the problem as a graph where states or elements represent vertices and relations represent edges.
Use Breadth-First Search (BFS) for shortest path/level order, or Depth-First Search (DFS) / Disjoint Set Union (DSU) for connectivity.
Track visited states with a hash set or boolean array to avoid cycles.
learningObjectives: Master algorithmic design for Redundant Connection Problem.
Understand time and space complexity trade-offs.
Implement robust edge-case handling for boundary conditions.
